newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba battens down as Lili approaches.
newsitem.headline: Cuba battens down as Lili approaches.

text.p: Cuba braced on Wednesday for the arrival of Tropical Storm Lili, declaring a hurricane emergency in some western areas and a hurricane alert in other areas as severe weather approached the island from the south.

Thousands of people were evacuated from their homes in Havana, where many houses are in poor condition, as a precautionary measure. Cuba's civil defense organization upgraded its preparations at mid-day, declaring a hurricane emergency for the provinces of Pinar del Rio, Havana and Matanzas and the Isle of Youth to the south.

The central provinces of Cienfuegos, Villa Clara, Sancti Spiritus and Ciego de Avila were on hurricane alert. Cuban weather forecasters said the storm was likely to cross the Isle of Youth early on Thursday, moving over western areas of Cuba during the day.
"There is a high danger for our country," forecaster Jose Rubiera told state television's mid-day news program.

The storm, with maximum sustained winds of 65 mph (105 kph), was likely to pass over Cuba at the upper limits of a tropical storm or as a hurricane, he said. Either way, heavy rains and very strong winds were expected.
At 11 p.m. EDT (0300 GMT), the center of Lili was located at latitude 18.7 north, longitude 84.5 west, about 325 miles (520 km) south-southwest of Havana.
The storm was drifting slowly to the north after remaining virtually stationary for much of the day, but forecasters expected it to pick up forward speed in the next day.

The Cuban government upgraded hurricane watches to hurricane warnings for the western provinces and the Isle of Youth. The Cayman Islands and the east coast of Mexico's Yucatan peninsula were under a tropical storm warning.
Forecasters in Miami said rainfall of 12 inches (30 cm) or more was possible.

In Havana, Communist Party First Secretary Esteban Lazo said some 88,000 people living in homes in poor condition in central and old Havana should be prepared to be evacuated to hostels or to stay with relatives from Wednesday afternoon.

There is an increased danger of houses collapsing in Havana with the onset of severe weather. Some 70 homes in poor and decaying condition have collapsed partially or totally in bad weather so far this year.

Some 30,000 Havana high school students resident at boarding schools in the countryside were being evacuated and some schools in Havana closed early on Wednesday as they were turned into hostels for people being evacuated. All schools in the city were scheduled to be closed on Thursday.
Workers began clearing debris from streets in Havana and removing rubbish from gutters. Citizens were urged to help clean up.

Cuba, slowly emerging from the worst of an economic crisis caused by the collapse of the former Soviet Union, could be badly hurt by a bad storm or hurricane. At this time of year, the key sugar cane crop, a crucial source of foreign exchange, is just two or three months away from being harvested.

The central provinces are huge sugar producing areas and the western province of Pinar del Rio is where most of the island's tobacco crop is grown. In early 1993, a fierce storm in Havana and surrounding areas caused extensive damage to homes and crops.
